headline: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.voteItem: Motion to enter executive session on DRIP 9.12, the proposed acquisition of an irrigation company's water infrastructure assets
meeting.summary: The committee heard plans to move disaster survivors' interim housing to county programs and voted 7–0 to meet privately on water assets.
meeting.recap: The managing director said the mayor asked HIEMA to request a limited extension from FEMA.[[0:08:53]] Two interim housing sites will move to the Office of Recovery for three or four years while permanent homes are built.[[0:12:37]] The county is launching a rental assistance program for people who fall out of FEMA lease help.[[0:15:07]] A public campaign on moving from FEMA to the Office of Recovery program has not launched yet.[[0:19:51]] The housing director said the state plans a new notice moving one site's move-out date closer to the end of February.[[0:21:00]] Officials said a project on a slide was mislabeled as Lahaina housing and will be corrected.[[0:34:04]] An official said a FEMA program approved just before the meeting lets FEMA transfer temporary units to the state or county.[[0:40:00]] The committee voted 7–0 to go into executive session (a closed-door meeting) on a proposed purchase of an irrigation company's water assets.[[0:52:06]] The chair deferred the item without further discussion.[[0:56:20]]
decided: The motion passed 7–0, with two members excused.
The chair deferred the item because the committee had to leave the room.
meeting.next: The county will launch a public campaign on how to move from FEMA to the Office of Recovery program. Staff will correct the mislabeled slide and resubmit it. Officials said they can come back to discuss specific housing solutions, including for unsheltered residents.

moments.q: "they tend to call it like the FEMA cliff"
"literally just today, we got the approval"
Vote to enter executive session: "seven ayes, zero nos"

issues.why: Officials said the concern is what happens to households in existing programs if FEMA stops providing help.
